Fixed. Root cause in src/interval.js: Interval.fromISO called DateTime.fromISO(s/e, opts) directly, so with Settings.throwOnInvalid = true a non-date component (e.g. the duration part of "2016-01-01/P1Y") threw InvalidDateTimeError instead of falling through to the Duration.fromISO branch / Interval.invalid(). Now each DateTime.fromISO call is guarded and validity flags drive the branching, so valid duration-based intervals parse and invalid input honours throwOnInvalid (throwing InvalidIntervalError). Verified: test/interval suite 127/127 pass; full suite unchanged apart from 2 pre-existing ICU-related toFormat failures that also fail on the untouched baseline.

Fixed. Root cause in src/impl/util.js objToLocalTS(): the years-0..99 workaround only re-applied the year via setUTCFullYear(getUTCFullYear() - 1900), after Date.UTC had already normalized month/day overflow using the 19XX calendar. Since 2000 is a leap year but 100 is not, dates rolling past Dec 31 came out a day early (e.g. 0099-12-31 + 62 days gave 0100-03-02 instead of 0100-03-03). Now it sets year, month and day together (setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)) so normalization happens in the target year. Verified: test/datetime/math.test.js 47/47 pass, plus 1.8M cross-checked plus/minus cases with 0 mismatches; full suite unchanged except the 2 pre-existing ICU-related toFormat failures.

Fixed. Root cause in src/impl/util.js padStart(): it padded the whole stringified number including the minus sign, so negative years came out as "00-1-01-01" / "-100-01-01". Now the sign is emitted separately and only the magnitude is zero-padded to the requested width, giving -0001-01-01, -0100-01-01, -118040-05-25, while +10000-01-01 and wide values stay unchanged. Verified against a pristine-HEAD baseline: 892 passed / 2 failed both before and after (the 2 failures are the pre-existing ICU-related French toFormat hour-padding cases), so no green test regressed.

Fixed. Root cause in src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js: get isValid() was hard-coded to true, so FixedOffsetZone.instance('foo') / new FixedOffsetZone('foo') reported a valid zone with a NaN offset, and DateTimes placed in it stayed valid. Now isValid returns isNumber(this.fixed) (mirroring IANAZone's self-validation convention), so such zones are invalid and DateTimes in them are invalid ("unsupported zone"). Verified: test/zones 32/32 pass, valid fixed zones (utcInstance, instance(0), parseSpecifier) unaffected, and a revert-and-rerun confirmed the only 2 full-suite failures are the pre-existing ICU French toFormat ones.
